title: Wilhelm cracks the ritual integration over the winter
notes: Wilhelm's winter work at Carrick: the folk system stops being spontaneous-only. He judges the formulaic-ritual step 'really easy — someone just needed to point it out'; the remaining work is formalizing the Artes Liberales / Philosophiae contribution.
source: Session recap 2026-07-25 (Ars Magica transcript), winter-1223 downtime.
body_text:
Wintering at **Carrick** while his research assistants are out gathering material, Wilhelm spends the season on **integration and research** — turning his folk system from a curiosity into something with proper mechanics.
**The breakthrough he's most confident about:** his current system knows only **spontaneous, ritual-style casting** (roll halved). Proper **formulaic** magic would let a caster add **Artes Liberales** and **Philosophiae** to the effort *and* drop the divide-by-two — roughly tripling the effective pool. Over the winter he works out that this ritual integration is, in his own estimate, **"really easy — someone just needed to point it out"**: give a caster the finished formula rather than making them improvise it each time.
**The Artes Liberales angle** is the part still taking his time: the obvious-once-said refinements a folk caster never bothered to name. If a ceremony wants a circle, it helps to know **geometry** enough to draw a true one; if it wants words of power, it helps to know **rhetoric** enough to project the voice. Formalizing how Artes Liberales and Philosophiae feed the working is the winter's real labor.
**Logistics.** His assistants are sent west and south to gather hedge-magic insight, carrying **sacks of grain and silver** as payment for anyone willing to teach the "easy stuff." Wilhelm writes letters — to the loose **wizard-circle** he keeps looped in on the project, to his family, and to **Dietrich** (his brother/scribe, back at his teaching post), whom he promises a **tractatus of the generated folk-magic spells** once it's finished. He intends to set up a **lab on shore** (he is chronically seasick and will not stay aboard ship an hour longer than he must), and has arranged for his research materials to be relocated from home toward wherever the covenant next bases itself. Feeds t019, t009, and the mundane vis-factory pitch (t020).

title: Regiones the Third: the frog-folk ambush (cliffhanger)
notes: s16 reached (cliffhanger). The murfolk (frog-folk) confirmed as the Level-3 colony. Session ended here; next session opens on the ambush.
body_text:
Crossing into Level 3: a bioluminescent marsh — fungi above and below the water, paths that dip between deep pools, and **underwater 'homesteads'** framed in light, with figures moving in the depths.
An arrow lands at Garrett's feet; a dart strikes Dagmar's neck and drops him into a hallucinatory (not unconscious) state. As he goes under he locks eyes with the shooter — not a merman like Ka'wa'ill but a grotesque, intelligent **frog-fish person** (the murfolk).
Ambush sprung; the scene is paused here — next session opens on dealing with it.

title: Valdemar pitches an Isle-of-Man base — and the covenant authorizes it
notes: Split from the former p078 'base revealed' event (owner review 2026-08-23): the Winter 1221-22 pitch + authorization. Leads into the Summer 1222 survey ('Establishing a dock and base on the Isle of Man', now Incomplete) and the Spring 1224 arrival (p078).
body_text:
Wintering in Bruges is expensive and yields little, so over the winter Valdemar proposes the covenant establish an anchorage of its own — a remote place to winter, haul ships up for repair, and house grog families — funded largely by his own piracy rather than the covenant purse.
He argues for seeking the local lord's PERMISSION and legitimate title rather than squatting a pirate's cove ('permission rather than forgiveness'), and asks for ~50 Mythic pounds to start (of a ~130£ full estimate — 5£ quarters per magus, 1£ per grog family, plus construction).
The magi debate: Dagmar is wary of tying resources to a stationary site (the covenant is deliberately mobile) unless it sits on a strong Magic aura they can claim; Éogan is for it if it pays its way; all agree it must generate income, not be a financial sink.
Peripheral-Code note raised: magi may not swear fealty or serve as court wizards, but may hold a landed site; the Isle of Man's jurisdictional grey zone — not clearly in any Tribunal — is a feature Valdemar sought.
The covenant authorizes the venture; Valdemar will scout and establish it.

title: The murfolk ambush, fought to a retreat
notes: Resolves the p086 cliffhanger. The negotiation of s16 did not happen — it went straight to a fight, then a withdrawal.
body_text:
Past Tormente and the aligned second chamber, the party enters **Level 3**: a bioluminescent, shin-deep marsh with lit homesteads under the water. The murfolk spring their ambush — a dart in Dagmar's neck (he is the least combat-capable), arrows and barbed spears from the reeds, and a **coral-staff shaman that summons a water elemental**.

The fight turns on a handful of strokes. **Pieter** cuts the dart out of Dagmar's neck; Dagmar's Stamina holds (a natural 18), and the venom takes him the *other* way — an innervating dose rather than a poison, **+3 to defense for the encounter**. **Llewellyn's Ball of Abysmal Flame** kills murfolk outright — they have no resistance worth the name against his penetration. **Dagmar** spontaneously casts Call to Slumber and drops the shaman. **Valdemar's** Hermetic attempt to command the water elemental fails; switching to **viktir Norse magic (the Laguz rune)** he restrains it instead — its water turned to wet cement. **Foxglove** is cut down to two heavy wounds and barely stabilized.

Dagmar calls the retreat. Killing through the colony is possible but ruinous; the covenant's people are bleeding.

title: The upper path and the empty throne
notes: Level 4 reached — not through the colony but around it. Confirms the throne is empty and the deeper passage (Level 5) is locked.
body_text:
Dagmar's Piercing the Magic Veil shows a **second entrance above the one they came through**, a kept-but-unwalked path where the evidence of murfolk stops. It climbs out of the water into a cavern: a long drop to dark water, a **radiant quartz bridge with its own inner light**, a **giant nautilus shell** at the center, and a **magnificent, empty throne**. Planetary symbols hang in an arc above it, as in the second chamber — and, like there, they **drift subtly, tracking the true spheres**.

The aura here reads *weaker* than the colony below — magic at ebb, as if tidal. The passage on is a locked way into the deeper regio. The room is pristine, expectant, abandoned.

title: The scent that is missing — Solving's disappearance echoed
notes: Links the Carnac regio to Solving's vanishing and to the Bruges anomaly. Feeds the Solving thread.
body_text: Working the throne room with a spontaneous **examine-the-regio** casting, Dagmar's sensory tests return **nothing for smell** — his own scent is being **leeched off him**, a gap where a sense should be. He recognizes it twice over: from **Bruges**, and from the space where **Solving vanished**, which the grogs led him to years ago — a place that was not electric or ozone-touched but *clean*, missing its natural smell. The same absence is here, in a regio whose magic runs tidal and whose deepest door is a gateway.

title: The conjunction dated, and Llewellyn stays behind
notes: Sets the March 1226 clock in play and parks Llewellyn at Carnac until it. Ties s18.
body_text: Reading the throne's drifting spheres against Abu Ma'shar's work on the great conjunctions, **Llewellyn** places the next one: **Spring 1226**. The regio's magic is cyclical and at ebb; the deeper door is keyed to that conjunction, not to the constant aura. Rather than leave and lose the thread, **Llewellyn elects to remain in the regio** — sustaining himself by magic — to be present when the way opens. Dagmar judges the party too hurt to press on, and undertakes to **return by the conjunction**, well under a year and a half off. From Autumn 1224, the clock reads to Spring 1226.

title: Tormente defers its price for the gold
notes: Closes the Tormente errand and puts the dragon-gold brokering on hold. Bears on t072 / s19.
body_text: Exiting past **Tormente**, the party finds it content — it does not ask after the member left behind. Dagmar raises the gold again: Tormente had expressed interest in trading it for something from the outside world. Asked what it wants, the dragon answers only **"Ask me in a few years."** The brokering is not refused, only deferred; the covenant will convert the five bags on its own account in the meantime.

scene: Isle of Man — the grant, recounted
title: The Isle-of-Man title: Rǫgnvaldr's lifetime grant
notes: Fills in how Valdemar holds the Isle-of-Man land. Resolves t081.
body_text: The lord Valdemar dealt with is **Rǫgnvaldr (Reginald), King of Man and the Isles** — Norse-Gaelic, a fair ruler whose island has stayed out of open conflict, though a rival **brother** angles for it. Valdemar offered presence and a taxpaying settlement, no fealty and no English alliance; the king, wanting a quiet defensive asset, agreed. The terms: the land is Valdemar's **for his lifetime only, not heritable**, sealed by a **Christian oath sworn on God's name not to ally with the king's enemies** — no court-wizard service. Valdemar, viktir and no Christian, gives the oath and means to keep his word regardless. The lack of a church in the settlement is left unremarked; with Father Lachlan and Christian covenfolk building there, one will come.

title: The Tide of Memory's unsigned enchantments
notes: New small mystery; complicates the assumption that Solving built the ship's items.
body_text: Éogan and Dagmar go looking for paperwork on the **custom magic items aboard the Tide of Memory** and find none. The likelier reading is that they **came with the ship** or were made by a covenant magus **before** the current company — not, as Dagmar had assumed, by **Solving**.

title: Éogan teaches Aquam; Valdemar and Dagmar study it
notes: The winter lesson at the Isle-of-Man lab. Foundry XP: Valdemar Aquam+12, Dagmar Aquam+7, Éogan Teaching+2 (covenant service).
body_text: His Hermetic command of the water elemental having failed where his viktir working held it, **Valdemar** resolves to lean into the form the Isle-of-Man lab most favors. **Éogan** — the covenant's strongest Aquam magus — teaches **Aquam** over the winter; **Valdemar** (declining to take the harder viktir-conversion route, this time learning Aquam straight) and **Dagmar** both study under him. It is Éogan's covenant service for the year.
